title: Optical Overlay Metrology - Micro-cracks Detection on Surfscan SP5
subtitle: Post-Etch Quality Validation for 14nm Node Manufacturing
author: Lisa Johansson

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Surfscan SP5 system to detect and classify Micro-cracks defects during post-etch inspection at the 14nm technology node. The test is conducted at Singapore Fab 7 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Micro-cracks defects that are critical to yield at the 14nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Surfscan SP5 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Surfscan SP5
- Inspection Type: Optical Overlay Metrology
- Target Defect: Micro-cracks
- Process Step: Post-Etch
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 14nm
- Fab Location: Singapore Fab 7

This test case applies to all Surfscan SP5 systems deployed at Singapore Fab 7 for post-etch monitoring in the 14nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Surfscan SP5
Software Version: v14.2.722
Recipe: OPTICAL_OVERLAY_METROLOGY_14nm_POST_ETCH
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: High (77 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 5mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Surfscan SP5 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Optical Overlay Metrology' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Micro-cracks defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 14nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 54 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 92% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.0% for Optical Overlay Metrology
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.93 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-01-19
Wafers Tested: 46
Total Defects Found: 3942
Defect Density: 557.68 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 5.1%
Capture Rate: 89.9%
Test Duration: 69 minutes
System Uptime: 97.8%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Surfscan SP5 demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Micro-cracks at the 14nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Minor calibration drift was detected after extended run; re-calibration resolved the issue.

e) Statistical process control charts showed stable performance over the test period.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
